errorCodes.meaning: The embedded Data Integrity proof does not verify — a bad signature, a verification method not controlled by the statement's `issuer`, or one not in the issuer's current `authentication` relationship.
The member DID could not be resolved now, so the statement could not be checked. Retry later.
The statement's `audience` is not this mediator's DID.
The statement's `iat` is more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.
The statement's `exp` lies further after `iat` than the mediator accepts for a revoke-all statement.
The statement names an epoch later than the member DID's current one. `details.currentEpoch` carries the epoch in force; re-sign under it.
The member DID's record changed under concurrent writes too many times for the epoch advance to be committed. Nothing changed; send the request again.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MuxDataIntegrityProof.description: The W3C Data Integrity proof embedded in a mux statement, made by the member DID: the format and verifier Trust Tasks already use for document proofs (SPEC §4.7). The proof covers the whole statement except `proof` itself, as the cryptosuite defines. Closed: a member Data Integrity defines but this list omits is refused.

created.description: OPTIONAL: when the proof was made, as Data Integrity defines it. Covered by the proof; the statement's own `iat` is what the mediator checks.

cryptosuite.description: The W3C Data Integrity EdDSA cryptosuite used.

proofPurpose.description: MUST be `authentication`. Any other value is refused with `messaging/mux:proofPurposeInvalid` — a proof made for another relationship (an `assertionMethod` credential signature, say) is never accepted as control of the DID.

verificationMethod.description: The DID URL of the verification method that signed. MUST be controlled by the statement's `issuer` and listed in that DID's current `authentication` relationship.

MuxDataIntegrityProof.title: MuxDataIntegrityProof

MuxDid.description: A DID, carried verbatim and compared by exact string equality. Unlike the messaging family's `Vid`, never a hash: the mediator resolves it to verify a statement signed by it. For a member DID reached over TSP, the TSP VID is the DID itself.
MuxDid.title: MuxDid

Response.description: The success response to a messaging/mux/revoke-all request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/mux/revoke-all/0.1#response.

epoch.description: The member DID's epoch now in force; a new grant must carry it.

epochAdvanced.description: False when the epoch named in the proof had already been voided, so nothing changed.

revokedGrants.description: How many grants that were active this request moved to `epochRevoked`.

Response.title: Messaging — Mux Revoke All — response payload

RevokeAllStatement.description: A member DID's statement, proving current control of it, that every grant on it signed under `epoch` or earlier is void. Signed by the member with an embedded Data Integrity proof whose purpose is `authentication`.

audience.description: The mediator's DID. A statement names exactly one mediator and is refused by every other.

epoch.description: The epoch being voided: the member DID's current one.

exp.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2): when the statement stops being accepted. REQUIRED; MUST be after `iat` and in the future.

iat.description: JWT NumericDate (RFC 7519 §2), whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC: when the statement was signed. MUST NOT be more than 60 seconds in the mediator's future.

issuer.description: The member DID: the signer, and the DID the statement concerns.

type.description: Always `muxRevokeAll`; names the statement kind, so a statement of one kind is never accepted as another.

RevokeAllStatement.title: RevokeAllStatement

schema.description: A member DID, proving current control with a signed revoke-all statement, advances its epoch at the mediator and so voids every grant on it at once. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

revocation.description: The revoke-all statement; the member DID is its `issuer`.
